origin: cwe/121/cpp Key Principles: where a genuine upper bound exists, reject the oversized value rather than calling resize()

finding.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
finding.summary: The copy loop writes dataLen bytes into the 32-element, stack-resident payload std::array with no check that dataLen fits, overflowing payload through unchecked operator[] for any dataLen greater than 32.

trap: Clamping the loop bound to std::min(dataLen, frame.payload.size()) stops the write from overflowing payload but is an incomplete fix if frame.length is left set to the original dataLen: any caller that later reads frame.length bytes from frame.payload (to send or log it, for example) reads uninitialized bytes past what was actually copied - a fix that closes the write here can reopen a read overflow immediately downstream. Clamp both consistently: reject an oversized dataLen outright (matching the general preference to reject rather than silently resize or truncate), or clamp the loop bound and set frame.length to that same clamped count.
must_preserve: For dataLen <= payload.size(), buildFrame still copies all dataLen bytes into payload and sets frame.length to dataLen. A dataLen exceeding payload.size() is rejected or truncated consistently - frame.length always matches the number of bytes actually written to payload.
